title: AN ALTAR TO THE GOD OF ISRAEL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After Jacob came from Paddan Aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in Canaan and camped within sight of the city. For a hundred pieces of silver, he bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, the plot of ground where he pitched his tent. There he set up an altar and called it El Elohe Israel." - Gen 33:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last Jacob "arrived safely" back in the land of Canaan. That word safely is precious, for it marks a promise kept. Years before at Bethel, God had said, "I will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land" (Gen 28:15). Now, after twenty years, two families, a fortune in flocks, a night of wrestling, and a fearful reunion — Jacob is home, safe. God had done exactly what He said.

And how does Jacob respond? He buys a piece of ground and builds an altar, naming it El Elohe Israel — "God, the God of Israel." Notice the name: Jacob uses his new name, Israel, and confesses that the Lord is his God. The altar is a public declaration of who God is and to whom Jacob now belongs. Worship is his fitting response to God's faithfulness.

This is a good pattern for our lives too. When God brings us safely through a long, hard journey, the right response is not merely relief but worship. We build an "altar" — we stop to acknowledge God, to thank Him, to declare that He is our God.

Look back over your own journey. Where has God brought you "safely" when the way was uncertain? Let His faithfulness lead you to worship. Build your altar, and say with Jacob, "The Lord is my God."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God brought me "safely" through a hard journey?
2. Is worship my response to God's faithfulness, or just relief?
3. Can I declare, like Jacob, "The Lord is my God"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You for bringing me safely through hard journeys, just as You promised. I build my altar of worship to You and declare that You are my God. Amen.
